author: haacked
body:
blocking: ClickHouse doesn't preserve sub-query order through UNION ALL. The ORDER BY timestamp ASC lives inside the inner property sub-select, but the planner is free to interleave UNION-ALL branches in parallel, so the rows the Python loop iterates may not be chronological.
The loop downstream depends on chronological order: person_properties.update(set_properties) is last-write-wins, and $set_once is first-write-wins. Two $set events touching the same key can resolve to either value, non-deterministically.
The mock-based unit tests don't catch this because they hand-feed rows in a fixed order, and the integration test file now mocks sync_execute too (so nothing exercises the real query ordering).
Fix: project the timestamp out of the property sub-select and add a top-level ORDER BY:
query = f"""
SELECT kind, set_json, set_once_json, event_name, ts FROM (
    SELECT 1 AS kind,
           JSONExtractRaw(properties, '$set') AS set_json,
           JSONExtractRaw(properties, '$set_once') AS set_once_json,
           event AS event_name,
           timestamp AS ts
    FROM events
    WHERE team_id = %(team_id)s AND distinct_id IN %(distinct_ids)s
        AND timestamp >= %(lower_bound)s AND timestamp <= %(upper_bound)s
        AND ({event_filter})
    ORDER BY timestamp ASC LIMIT {int(row_limit)}
)
UNION ALL
SELECT kind, set_json, set_once_json, event_name, ts FROM (
    SELECT 0 AS kind, '' AS set_json, '' AS set_once_json, '' AS event_name, toDateTime(0) AS ts
    FROM events
    WHERE team_id = %(team_id)s AND distinct_id IN %(distinct_ids)s
        AND timestamp <= %(upper_bound)s LIMIT 1
)
ORDER BY kind ASC, ts ASC
"""
Then unpack kind, set_json, set_once_json, event_name, _ts = row in the loop. Existence rows have kind=0 so they sort first; the ts placeholder for the existence row doesn't matter once it's been consumed.
